title: Exec Escalations Weekly Digest — 2026 W07 (Draft)
content:
Weekly digest covering customer escalations and exec-facing decisions for 2026 W07.

Confidentiality / distribution
- Internal-only. Do not forward outside Redwood leadership + on-call/SRE/CS leadership.
- This digest avoids customer-sensitive logs and omits account-specific configuration details; see linked SUP tickets + call transcripts for full context.

Executive summary (W07)
- Total escalations opened/active this week: 6 (P0: 1, P1: 3, P2: 2)
- SLA misses: 0 confirmed
- SLA near-misses: 2 (both due to update cadence drift while “Waiting on Eng”)
- Status page events: 1 partial regional degradation (eu-west embeddings timeouts) — posted after approval flow
- Primary themes: streaming reliability + customer retry behavior; Dedicated autoscaling stability; Private upgrade diagnostics; audit log delivery latency; quota / rate-limit header confusion
- Credits decisions: 1 pending exec approval, 1 declined (insufficient evidence of SLA breach), 2 “not requested / pre-emptively monitored”

SLA & comms highlights
- Update cadence: We are aligning on enterprise update cadence language (“every 60 minutes minimum during active mitigation; more frequently if user-visible changes or ETA shifts”). Two near-misses occurred where comms paused while waiting for engineering confirmation; resolved via Rachel + Owen pushing a structured update (“what we know / what we’re doing / next update time”).
- Bridging: Support bridge creation is improving, but we still have inconsistent pinning of related SUP tickets and missing request ID bundles in the first 15 minutes.

Escalation details

1) Streaming connection resets / timeouts (Enterprise, Hosted API)
- Ticket(s): SUP-1842 (primary), related: SUP-1854
- Severity/priority: P0 (customer labeled as production outage; partial mitigation available)
- Customer impact: Intermittent stream resets mid-generation; downstream application retries amplified load; elevated support volume + exec attention.
- Timeline (high level):
  - Trigger: multiple reports within same hour across us-east streaming traffic.
  - Mitigation: recommended client-side retry/backoff + timeout tuning; interim networking guidance; on-call confirmed no full-region outage but identified elevated disconnect rate.
  - Comms: enterprise email cadence maintained after first hour; customer requested a more explicit “safe retry policy” statement for their incident channel.
- Current status: Improving; monitoring ongoing. Support macro + known-issue article drafted and being finalized to reduce repeated back-and-forth.
- SLA / near-miss: Near-miss on update cadence during “Waiting on Eng” window (resolved same day).
- Credits: Pending customer ask; we will not offer proactively without confirming SLA breach and scope of impact.
- Engineering follow-ups:
  - ENG-4822 / redwood/pr-19321: improve streaming disconnect error detail and request ID propagation (in review).
  - ENG-4827 + SDK docs PRs: publish streaming troubleshooting guidance consistently across SDKs (Python/TS/Go).
  - Support request: clearer dashboard signal for streaming health that Support can cite without deep SRE context.

2) Dedicated autoscaling oscillation causing latency spikes (Dedicated)
- Ticket(s): SUP-1844; related capacity questions: SUP-1853
- Severity/priority: P1
- Customer impact: Latency spikes during peak; customer observed frequent replica churn; concern about meeting their internal SLOs.
- Root cause (summary): Autoscaling policy parameters too aggressive for workload burst pattern; scale-down behavior induced oscillation.
- Mitigation: Temporary config changes (cooldowns/min replicas) applied with SRE guidance; customer saw stabilization within the day.
- Current status: Stable under current settings; long-term guardrails in progress.
- SLA: No misses. Comms were timely; we should replicate this playbook.
- Credits: Not requested.
- Engineering follow-ups:
  - ENG-4829: autoscaling stability guardrails (cooldowns + min capacity enforcement) — scheduled.
  - ENG-4823: add canonical dashboard links to support-safe runbooks so Support can confirm oscillation quickly.

3) Private installer upgrade stuck at migrations (Private / on-prem style deployment)
- Ticket(s): SUP-1845
- Severity/priority: P1
- Customer impact: Upgrade blocked; customer paused rollout; compliance team concerned about rollback safety + auditability.
- Mitigation: Safe rollback steps provided; collected installer logs + cluster events per checklist; engineering engaged for diagnostics.
- Current status: Customer unblocked via rollback; awaiting next maintenance window with improved diagnostics bundle.
- SLA: No misses.
- Credits: Not requested.
- Engineering follow-ups:
  - ENG-4828 / redwood-private-installer/pr-566: diagnostics bundle + clearer failure hints (in progress).
  - Docs: Ensure workaround article clearly flags “temporary mitigation” vs “supported upgrade path” and includes “when to escalate” to Private Deployments.

4) Audit log delivery latency (Enterprise)
- Ticket(s): SUP-1846
- Severity/priority: P1
- Customer impact: Audit events delayed (reported >30 minutes). Customer uses audit logs for compliance monitoring and alerts; asked for clarity on delivery expectations.
- Root cause (summary): Pipeline backlog under load; alerting thresholds were not aligned to enterprise expectations.
- Mitigation: Provided interim guidance for export window + retry behavior; SRE confirmed backlog and recovery trend; comms focused on what’s changing operationally.
- Current status: Monitoring; improvements underway.
- SLA / near-miss: Near-miss on update cadence due to waiting for an “approved” root-cause line; resolved by using the approved comms template (impact + mitigations + next update time, with RCA deferred).
- Credits: Customer asked about credits in principle; we requested a concrete impact statement and will evaluate against contract terms.
- Engineering follow-ups:
  - ENG-4824 / observability-pack/pr-711: first-class lag metric + alert thresholds + dashboard and runbook links (in review).
  - Process: Establish an “expected audit log delivery SLO” statement that Support can quote consistently (must be contract-safe; Legal review).

5) Unexpected 429s / rate-limit header inconsistency (Hosted API)
- Ticket(s): SUP-1843, SUP-1855
- Severity/priority: P2
- Customer impact: Elevated 429s post-SDK upgrade; confusion caused by header messaging; increased ticket churn.
- Mitigation: Support validated account limits + telemetry; shared workaround guidance (interpretation of headers + SDK config checks).
- Current status: Fix in progress; doc workaround will reduce repeat tickets.
- SLA: No issues.
- Credits: Declined (not an outage; behavior within quota constraints once configuration corrected).
- Engineering follow-ups:
  - ENG-4825 / redwood/pr-19322: header consistency + tests (in progress).
  - Docs/DevEx: ensure troubleshooting page links directly from SDK upgrade notes and from Support macros.

6) Embeddings timeouts (eu-west) — incident comms alignment case
- Ticket(s): SUP-1850
- Severity/priority: P1
- Customer impact: Increased timeouts for embeddings requests in eu-west; customers experienced partial degradation.
- Actions: Bridge created; moved to #incidents after SRE confirmation; status page update posted following approval flow.
- Current status: Resolved; monitoring.
- SLA: No misses.
- Credits: Not requested this week.
- Follow-ups:
  - Confirm we consistently link SUP tickets into incident channels (bot prompt is coming via incident-bot/pr-209).
  - Ensure known-issues index points to the correct “regional degradation” comms expectations vs “workaround” docs.

Open risks / watch list
- “Waiting on Customer” and SLA timers: We still have ambiguity in when we pause internal SLA timers vs continue update cadence. Recommendation: keep update cadence even when waiting on customer if the incident is ongoing or customer impact likely persists; clearly state what we need and what we are doing meanwhile.
- Bypassing on-call: A few pings to individual engineers happened before paging the correct rotation. We need to reinforce the escalation matrix and keep the process consistent.

Decisions needed from leadership
1) Credits policy consistency: For enterprise incidents where impact is intermittent (e.g., streaming disconnects) we need a consistent standard for evidence (request IDs + error rates + duration) before offering credits. Request: reaffirm that credits require (a) confirmed SLA breach per contract and (b) documented timeline in SUP ticket.
2) Audit log expectations statement: Approve a contract-safe, customer-facing wording for “expected audit log delivery latency” for enterprise customers, with Legal review (Sofia) and Security input (Naomi).

Engineering follow-ups (roll-up)
- Metrics & dashboards:
  - ENG-4823: add canonical dashboard links into runbooks; create Support-safe “quick view” dashboards.
  - ENG-4821: add/clarify metrics that indicate fallback routing activation to help Support confirm mitigations.
- Reliability fixes:
  - ENG-4824: audit log lag metric + alerting.
  - ENG-4829: Dedicated autoscaling stability guardrails.
  - ENG-4825: fix quota/rate-limit mismatch and header consistency.
  - ENG-4822 / redwood/pr-19321: improve streaming disconnect error details.
- Process tooling:
  - ENG-4830 / incident-bot/pr-209: prompt for + pin SUP ticket links in bridges.

Support/CS process follow-ups (next week)
- Publish/refresh: known-issues index + top workaround articles; ensure each includes “when to escalate” and is linked from Support macros.
- Jira hygiene: enforce required fields (region, model, SDK version, request IDs) at triage; ensure Slack thread links are present on P0/P1.
- Adoption check: quick 15-min refresher for Support on the bridge template + update cadence language.

Appendix: metrics (internal, early)
- Ticket deflection: too early for conclusive week-over-week; early signal is fewer duplicate “streaming timeout” follow-ups once we provided copy/paste-ready retry guidance.
- Time-to-triage: improved when request IDs were provided in first contact; still variable when customers provide only screenshots.

Owner notes (Jasmine)
- Please route any exec questions back through Dev Patel + Rachel Kim so we keep customer comms consistent and avoid conflicting timelines. If you need a one-paragraph exec summary for a specific account, ping us and we’ll produce a contract-safe version.
